desc:
Sales tax, VAT and multi-currency billing setup, delivered by Ecom Swift LLC. We switch on your payment provider's tax tools, add the currencies your customers expect and collect tax IDs from business buyers, with settings your accountant can confirm.

## What does tax and currency setup cover?

Tax and currency setup covers two related questions. First, in which currency does a customer see and pay the price? Second, is tax added, and at what rate? Providers such as Stripe offer tools that calculate and collect tax based on where the customer is and what you sell. They can also record a business buyer's tax ID and show the tax as a line on the invoice.

The setup requires inputs only you can give: where your business is based, which product types you sell and where you have registered or plan to register for tax. The tools then apply that information at checkout.

## Why this matters once you sell across borders

A customer in another country may expect to pay in their own currency, and may be put off by a price in a currency they must convert in their head. A business buyer may refuse to pay an invoice without their tax ID on it. A customer who sees a surprise tax line at the last step of checkout may abandon the purchase. Each of these problems is avoidable with clear setup.

The other side is risk. Tax rules differ between places and change over time. Collecting the wrong amount, or none, can cause trouble later. For that reason we set up the tools and settings, and your accountant confirms the rules. Ecom Swift LLC is not a tax adviser, and we do not tell you where you must register.

## What a good setup includes

- The provider's tax tool switched on and linked to your business address.
- Tax categories assigned to each product, so the correct rate applies.
- Tax shown clearly at checkout and again on every invoice.
- A tax ID field for business buyers, with reverse charge handling where the provider supports it.
- Selling currencies added for the regions you serve.
- Local price points that you choose, instead of raw exchange rate conversions.
- Currency chosen from the visitor's location, with a way to change it.
- Test orders from several locations, to confirm the right tax and currency appear.
- A settings sheet that your accountant can read and approve.
- A monthly tax summary export for bookkeeping.

## How we work

We start with a short conversation about where you sell and what you sell. Then we configure the provider's tax settings and test them. The Basic package turns on the tax tool, assigns product categories, shows tax on checkout and invoices and gives you a settings sheet for your accountant. The Standard package adds a second selling currency, a tax ID field for business buyers, reverse charge handling where supported, a tax line on each invoice and test orders from three locations. The Premium package adds several selling currencies, local price points, currency selection from the visitor's location, a monthly tax summary export and a handover call.

Currency prices can be fixed in each currency or converted from a base price. We explain the difference, because fixed local prices stay stable when exchange rates move, while converted prices follow the market. Which route you take is your choice.

## Do and avoid

**Do:**
- Share the settings sheet with your accountant before going live.
- Choose local price points that look natural in each currency.
- Show tax-inclusive or tax-exclusive prices consistently.
- Test orders from at least one location that should have tax and one that should not.
- Add currencies in stages, starting with your biggest markets.

**Avoid:**
- Guessing which regions require tax collection.
- Converting prices automatically in a way that gives odd amounts.
- Letting business buyers pay without a way to enter their tax ID.
- Changing a product's tax category after launch without a check.
- Treating a provider's tool as legal advice.

## Who this suits

This service suits a SaaS business whose first customers abroad have started asking for invoices with tax. It suits a company that wants to show prices in euros, pounds or other currencies instead of one. It also suits a founder who has a registration plan from an accountant and needs the checkout to follow it.

## What we need from you

Send your business address, the places where you plan to collect tax, the currencies you want and the product types you sell. Your accountant's advice on registrations is very helpful. We need a team role in your provider account and developer access to your app, never your passwords. After ordering, you receive a short checklist and a set of test orders to review.
